root.name: Philidor Defense: Berger Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 Be7 6. Be2 O-O 7. O-O c5 8. Nf3 Nc6 9. Bg5 Be6 10. Re1

overview: Black has castled and set up ...c5 against the Philidor structure, with ...Nc6 and ...Be6 developing sensibly. White has space and a lead in activity and usually plays Re1, Bg5 and Nd5 ideas. Black accepts a slightly passive game for a solid, undamaged position.

white_ideas.idea: Use the space advantage with Bg5, Re1 and Nd5

black_ideas.idea: Neutralise with ...h6 and ...Bxf3 or ...d5 at the right time
Keep the pawn structure intact and wait for a freeing ...d5

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on d6 and c5 against White's e4
Knight on d5 outpost fought over

character.notes: Black's setup is compact with few tactical weaknesses.

soundness.notes: The Philidor is respectable for Black.

structure.notes: Pawn tension with d6/c5 against e4; centre not locked.

level.notes: Straightforward development plans with some middlegame subtlety.
